title: Japan household spending fell 3.6% in real terms in July — the eighth straight yearly decline
summary: Japan's Statistics Bureau says two-or-more-person households spent an average ¥301,245 in July 2026. Real consumption fell 3.6% from a year earlier, compared with a 3.3% decline in June, although seasonally adjusted spending rose 0.5% from June.
why_it_matters: The year-on-year signal still shows weak household purchasing power, but the monthly improvement means the story is not simply straight-line deterioration. The next test is whether real wages and spending can turn positive together rather than households merely reshuffling categories.

sources.title: Family Income and Expenditure Survey — July 2026

claims.text: Average consumption expenditure for two-or-more-person households was ¥301,245 in July 2026.
claims.basis: Statistics Bureau monthly Family Income and Expenditure Survey

claims.text: Real household spending fell 3.6% year on year in July while seasonally adjusted real spending rose 0.5% from June.
Reuters described July as the eighth consecutive year-on-year decline and reported a market forecast of a 1.6% fall.

evidence_for: Real spending fell 3.6% year on year in July, a deeper decline than June's 3.3% fall.
The July result was weaker than the 1.6% decline expected in the Reuters poll.
Real income for workers' households also remained negative year on year in the official release.
evidence_against: Seasonally adjusted real consumption increased 0.5% from June.
Some discretionary categories, including travel, eating out and games, reportedly increased, showing uneven rather than universal weakness.
content.connection: The data are consistent with continued household price sensitivity: nominal spending can remain substantial while inflation erodes real purchasing power. The decisive next connection is whether wage gains begin to exceed household inflation on a sustained basis.
content.alternative_explanation: Monthly household-spending data can be moved by weather, timing and category mix. One weak year-on-year print alone is not proof of an economy-wide recession or a permanent deterioration in consumption.

content.what_would_change_mind: A sustained sequence of positive real household spending together with positive real household income would weaken the consumer-squeeze thesis materially.
content.implications: Value-seeking behavior and resistance to discretionary price increases are likely to remain important for retailers and household budgeting until real incomes improve more consistently.
content.history: Reuters' reading of the official data puts July at eight consecutive months of negative year-on-year real household spending.
